intro: Q2 2026 closes today. The structural thesis landscape is dominated by three converging forces: (1) the HBM AI memory supercycle — validated by Micron Q3 FY26 +15.7% beat, HBM4 sold-out through 2026, and Samsung's $226B AI data center commitment; (2) the FOMC Warsh hawkish pivot (3.80% median year-end, cuts to 2027-2028) reshaping the rate-sensitive discount rate for long-duration growth assets; and (3) the geopolitical-to-institutional transition in US tech policy (SCOTUS upholding Fed independence June 29 removes a key tail risk). The structural multi-quarter framework shifts from 'can the AI capex cycle sustain itself?' to 'which companies capture the monetization layer?' NVDA, MU, SK Hynix, MSFT, META, and GOOGL are the primary structural beneficiaries; BTC and SPCX carry structural theses that are binary on regulatory and macro outcomes.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.idea: NVDA is the dominant structural AI infrastructure pick despite the mandatory exit triggered by Stop Day 2 ($194.97 June 29 close). The institutional distribution above $195 is a near-term tactical overhang, not a structural thesis change. The Blackwell GPU platform (B200/B300 ramp through H2 2026), sovereign AI capex cycle ($100B+ multi-year government commitments), and HBM3e memory co-optimization moat remain intact. Q2 FY27 earnings August 26 ($91B quarterly revenue guide) is the next structural re-entry confirmation.
ideas.why: Every major AI model training and inference deployment in 2026 runs on NVIDIA hardware. The switching cost is 18-24 months of software re-optimization — AMD and Intel cannot close that gap in the FY27 timeframe. Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta are all committed to multi-year NVDA GPU purchases. The $195 supply overhang is from profit-taking at the ATH, not from fundamental deterioration.
ideas.driver: Blackwell B300 GPU ramp (H2 2026) expanding GPU compute density 3x vs. H100; sovereign AI capex from EU, Japan, Saudi Arabia, UAE creating demand backlog through 2028; inference demand scaling faster than training as AI moves from model development to deployment; August 26 Q2 FY27 earnings confirming or exceeding $91B quarterly guide
ideas.risk: US export controls tighten further restricting H20/B20 sales to China (removes ~$10-15B annual revenue); AMD MI400 achieves competitive performance within 12 months; hyperscaler capex cuts in H1 2027 if AI monetization disappoints; FOMC rate hold through 2027 compresses long-duration multiple

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.idea: MU is the most compelling near-term AI semi structural buy after Q3 FY26 +15.7% earnings beat (June 26). HBM4 sold out through 2026 and the $50B Q4 FY26 guide (~40% beat to prior consensus) removes execution uncertainty for the next two quarters. Unlike NVDA (distribution overhang) and SK Hynix (ADR overhang + Korean macro), MU has clean technical structure with no forced-selling pressure and a Q4 earnings catalyst in September that should confirm the HBM demand cycle duration.
ideas.why: Samsung's $226B AI data center commitment (June 29) validated MU's $50B Q4 guide at a national-government scale independent of US hyperscaler capex. The three-player HBM market (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron) is structurally oligopolistic — pricing discipline is enforced by technological complexity. Micron's US domestic manufacturing advantage (Idaho fab) provides geopolitical differentiation that Samsung and SK Hynix cannot match for US government AI procurement.
ideas.driver: HBM4 ramp through H2 2026 — $50B Q4 FY26 guide sets up FY27 at $200B+ annual revenue run rate; US CHIPS Act fab incentives reducing per-wafer cost at Idaho HBM4 production; DoD AI procurement mandates favoring US-manufactured HBM; September 2026 Q4 FY26 earnings confirmation of the HBM demand cycle
ideas.risk: HBM demand cycle peaks in H1 2027 earlier than expected as AI model efficiency improvements reduce memory per compute unit; Samsung or SK Hynix aggressive pricing to defend market share compresses MU margins despite volume growth; China export control escalation removes HBM export market; Q4 FY26 guide not achieved (volume shortfall or ASP compression)

ideas.name: SK Hynix
ideas.timeframe: 3-9 months (through Nasdaq ADR seasoning and Q3 2026 earnings)
ideas.idea: SK Hynix structural thesis: the world's largest HBM3e and HBM4 supplier ahead of Nasdaq ADR listing July 10 ($29.4B offering, underwritten by BofA/Goldman/Citigroup/JPMorgan). The ADR creates structural US institutional demand for a name that was previously accessible only via KRX 000660.KS or OTC ADR. Post-listing, index inclusion events (MSCI, S&P) drive systematic rebalancing buys over 3-6 months. Hold low conviction through the near-stop event resolution; add on confirmed KOSPI > 8,500 AND SK Hynix > ₩2,700,000 simultaneously.
ideas.why: SK Hynix supplies HBM3e exclusively to NVIDIA for H100/H200 systems and is ramping HBM4 for Blackwell. The supply relationship with NVDA gives SK Hynix structural revenue visibility through H2 2026. The Nasdaq ADR listing transforms the investor base from Korean retail + Asian institutional to global institutional — a permanent re-rating catalyst. The June 30 KST near-stop at ₩2,541,000 was absorbed by underwriter stabilization, consistent with a structural floor ahead of the ADR.
ideas.driver: July 10 Nasdaq ADR listing ($29.4B) — largest Korean company US listing ever; post-ADR index inclusions (MSCI, eventually S&P ADR index) driving systematic rebalancing demand; HBM4 ramp as primary supplier to NVDA Blackwell platform; Q3 2026 earnings (August) confirming HBM4 ASP premium over HBM3e
ideas.risk: June 30 KST close confirmed below ₩2,540,000 stop (triggered mandatory exit, thesis delayed 1-2 months); KOSPI macro deterioration (Korea won weakness, BoK rate hold) delays institutional inflows; ADR listing at discount to KRX price (IPO overhang); NVDA supply diversification reduces SK Hynix concentration premium

ideas.name: Microsoft Corporation
ideas.idea: Microsoft is the most diversified AI monetization play: Azure AI cloud (OpenAI partnership, exclusive enterprise deployment), Copilot productivity suite (365 seats at $30/month premium vs. $12/month base), and GitHub Copilot (developer workflow capture). FOMC hawkish hold to 2027-2028 pressures growth multiples but MSFT's $100B+ FCF generation and ~2% dividend yield provide a rate-resistant floor that pure-growth AI names lack.
ideas.why: Enterprise AI adoption is in the first innings — 2026 is about Copilot seat expansion, not new product launches. Each Copilot seat at $30/month is 2.5x the revenue of a base 365 seat, with higher gross margin (software vs. software). Azure AI workloads are sticky: once a Fortune 500 company's AI pipeline is on Azure, the switching cost (data migration + model re-training) is 12-24 months. The OpenAI exclusivity on Azure for enterprise fine-tuning is a 3-5 year structural moat.
ideas.driver: Copilot monetization at scale — 400M+ 365 commercial seats converting at 10-20% penetration to Copilot premium; Azure AI revenue compound at 35%+ YoY through FY27; GitHub Copilot Enterprise expansion (software dev workflow AI becoming standard); AI infrastructure licensing to sovereign AI programs (EU, Middle East)
ideas.risk: OpenAI partnership deteriorates (OpenAI explores independent cloud or direct enterprise relationships); Google Gemini captures enterprise AI adoption at lower price point; FOMC rate hold through 2028 compresses MSFT multiple from current 32x forward to 25x; EU AI Act compliance costs ($2-5B one-time) exceed estimates

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: META has the most direct AI-to-revenue conversion path of any big-tech name. AI ad targeting improvements are compounding: every 1% improvement in CTR translates directly to revenue without an enterprise sales cycle or contract renegotiation. LLaMA 4 open-source flywheel is accelerating third-party developer adoption, which creates a structural moat against closed-model competitors. The AI Reality Labs convergence (AR glasses, AI assistant integration) is a 2027-2028 option that is currently priced at near-zero.
ideas.why: 3.3B daily active users is an unassailable moat in AI training data and distribution. Every new AI feature (Llama-powered assistant, AI-generated ad creative, AI content ranking) reaches 3.3B users in real-time — the monetization feedback loop has zero lag. EU AI Act compliance is a cost, not an existential risk: META has the resources to comply while smaller European AI competitors cannot. The Zuckerberg AI personal assistant launch in 2026 is the first consumer AI product with genuine distribution at scale.
ideas.driver: AI ad efficiency compounding — CPM expansion from AI targeting improvements at 3.3B user scale; Llama 4 open-source ecosystem creating developer lock-in that monetizes through Meta AI products; AR glasses (Ray-Ban Meta) transitioning from niche to mainstream as AI assistant integration deepens; Q2 2026 earnings (late July) confirming AI monetization at scale
ideas.risk: Apple iOS privacy framework further restricts cross-app tracking (ATT 3.0 hypothetical); EU AI Act creates discriminatory compliance burden for US Big Tech; ad recession in H2 2026 if NFP weakness signals broader employment slowdown; AI Reality Labs losses exceed $20B/year, offsetting core business FCF generation

ideas.name: Alphabet Inc.
ideas.idea: GOOGL's June 29 Dow Jones inclusion (+5% first Dow day) marks a structural re-rating catalyst: the investor base expands to every Dow-tracking fund globally, creating a persistent systematic buyer floor. Waymo is the most mature autonomous vehicle deployment globally — SF and LA commercial operations, Phoenix expansion, and the NYC regulatory approval pending. Gemini AI integration into Search is the search-cannibalization risk that has kept GOOGL at a discount to peers; Q2 earnings will begin to clarify whether AI Mode increases or decreases per-search monetization.
ideas.why: GOOGL trades at a discount to META and MSFT on forward P/E because the market is pricing in Search AI cannibalization risk — if Gemini answers questions directly, users don't click ads. But the Q1 2026 data showed Search revenue accelerating, not decelerating, after AI Mode launch. The discount is a mispricing. Waymo at scale is a separate $100B+ business not valued in the current multiple. SCOTUS Fed independence ruling (June 29) removed the last major US regulatory overhang on Big Tech.
ideas.driver: Dow Jones inclusion systematic rebalancing demand (all 44 Dow-tracking ETFs must buy); Waymo commercial scaling — SF profitable unit economics demonstrated, NYC approval pending; Gemini AI Search monetization — higher-value AI ad placements offsetting organic click compression; Cloud Next 2026 (Q4) announcements on AI enterprise infrastructure
ideas.risk: DOJ antitrust search remedies (user choice screen mandates, default search restrictions) materially reduce Search revenue; Gemini AI Mode cannibalizes Search clicks faster than AI ads compensate; Waymo SF incident creates regulatory rollback; FOMC rate hold through 2028 compresses long-duration multiple (GOOGL trades at 24x, premium to value compresses)

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: Bitcoin's April 2024 halving created the supply shock that historically precedes a 12-18 month bull cycle peak. The post-halving cycle suggests a structural peak in mid-to-late 2026 or early 2027 at $120,000-$180,000. IBIT (BlackRock Bitcoin ETF) has institutionalized spot BTC demand — daily net flows now drive price more than miner selling. The current $59,339 price on Day 9 of the exit gate sequence is a tactical drawdown within an intact structural bull cycle. Re-entry after two consecutive UTC closes above $62,000 AND IBIT inflow resumption.
ideas.why: The halving math is binary: miner revenue drops 50%, forcing the weakest miners offline and permanently removing ~450 BTC/day of daily sell pressure. That supply shock takes 6-12 months to fully price in as exchange inventories normalize. IBIT net inflows represent institutional demand that did not exist in prior halving cycles — the 2024-2025 ETF approvals fundamentally changed the BTC demand structure. FOMC rate hold through 2027-2028 keeps real rates positive, which is a headwind, but institutional Bitcoin allocation is driven by portfolio diversification, not rate differentials.
ideas.driver: Post-halving supply shock fully pricing in through Q3-Q4 2026; IBIT inflow resumption post-NFP (institutional re-allocation to crypto after Q2 uncertainty resolves); US crypto regulatory clarity (SEC under new leadership 2026 formalizing spot ETF framework for ETH and SOL, legitimizing the asset class); El Salvador and sovereign adoption expanding (Bhutan, UAE strategic reserves)
ideas.risk: US Congress crypto legislation creates unfavorable tax treatment or leverage restrictions; IBIT sustained outflows for 10+ consecutive days signal institutional risk-off (not a short-term tactical exit); Mt. Gox trustee distribution (residual BTC claims) creates a second supply overhang wave; China mining ban reversal creates supply shock on the demand side (miner centralization risk)

ideas.name: SPCX (Space ETF)
ideas.timeframe: 3-12 months (through Nasdaq 100 inclusion and SpaceX IPO optionality)
ideas.idea: SPCX carries the most binary structural optionality in the portfolio: a SpaceX IPO (rumored 2026-2027) would cause SPCX to become the primary liquid ETF vehicle for retail SpaceX exposure, creating a structural inflow demand that is currently unquantifiable but potentially enormous. The Nasdaq 100 inclusion July 7 is the near-term structural catalyst. Re-entry gate: two consecutive closes above $185 after bond distribution clears (currently Day 6 of distribution from $25B June 26 settlement). Current step-aside HIGH conviction is tactical, not structural — the long-term thesis is intact.
ideas.why: Space infrastructure is entering the same inflection point that cloud computing crossed in 2012-2014: the cost curves have collapsed (Falcon 9 reuse, Starship development) but the revenue generation is still in its first commercial innings. Starlink is profitable. SpaceX's DoD contract backlog is $10B+. The SpaceX valuation at last private round ($210B+) implies significant upside for a public market re-rating if an IPO occurs. SPCX is the only ETF with material SpaceX exposure through secondary shares.
ideas.driver: SpaceX IPO optionality (2026-2027) — retail and institutional demand for liquid SpaceX exposure creates structural SPCX inflows; Nasdaq 100 inclusion July 7 — systematic rebalancing demand from QQQ and all Nasdaq 100 tracking products; Starlink terminal adoption acceleration in emerging markets; NASA Artemis II (crewed lunar flyby 2026) creating media-driven space sector sentiment
ideas.risk: SpaceX IPO delayed to 2028+ (private market remains dominant, removing the primary optionality catalyst); Nasdaq 100 inclusion demand fully absorbed in pre-inclusion window (June 30 window dressing) without post-inclusion follow-through; bond distribution second wave (another large block unwinds above $165, pushing back $185 gate timeline); DoD space contract reallocations away from SpaceX competitors in SPCX holdings
